title: Use a box plot to compare the spread of a few groups.
rule: Draw one row a group, its name and count of units flush left: a box from the first to the third quartile, the values a quarter and three quarters of the way up the ranked units, so the box holds the middle half; a 2 px line at the median, the middle unit; whiskers to the last unit within one and a half times the box’s length, and each unit beyond them as a small open circle. Print each median, give the group the title names the view’s red point while that red stays within 5 percent of the drawing (Rule 05.1), or the subject ink where Rule 14.6 sets ink in its place, as for a region of states, and say in the measure line what the box and whiskers span.
The chart draws from a table of each group’s quartiles, median and whiskers and a table of the units past the whiskers, so a chart of thousands of units stays light.
use_when: A reader who knows the form asks how widely a measure varies within each of a few groups, such as regions, and where the middle of each group sits.

use_instead.when: One group, and its shape matters more than its quartiles
Two groups or two years, and the reader compares their whole shapes
Each unit in a small group must stay visible

text: Five numbers a group, the two quartiles, the median and the whiskers’ two ends, let a reader compare many units across groups at a glance. The rule for the whiskers is fixed and stated, so an open circle past them always means the same thing, and no group’s spread depends on how the chart was drawn.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form box-plot: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s51; encode the five numbers and count; labels.outliers names the second dataset of units past the whiskers, labels.named the group in ink.
